stories.title: TRUMP: 'CLOSE TO ORDERING NEW STRIKES ON IRANIAN POWER PLANTS AND BRIDGES' — War Infrastructure Escalation in Real Time

The Qatar diplomatic track is a distraction — Qatar historically mediates when escalation is imminent, not when de-escalation is underway. The gap between market pricing (contained) and actual trajectory (expanding) is the widest it has been all day.

stories.title: SHELL CEO: HORMUZ DISRUPTIONS CAUSE 1.2 BILLION BARREL SUPPLY DEFICIT — The Market Has Not Priced This Number
stories.freshness: 11:23 UTC — 34 minutes ago. Shell CEO statement on Hormuz impact. No corresponding oil price move yet — massive gap between the number and the price.
stories.event: Shell CEO states publicly that events in the Strait of Hormuz have caused a 1.2 billion barrel supply deficit. For context: global oil consumption is ~100M barrels/day. 1.2 billion barrels = ~12 days of global consumption. Hormuz handles ~20M barrels/day in normal times. The blockade has been in effect for ~80 days. Even a partial blockade over 80 days creates enormous cumulative deficit. The Shell CEO is the first major oil executive to quantify this number publicly. This comes alongside: (1) Brent still trading sub-$90. (2) Indonesia raised fuel 32% — first EM demand destruction signal. (3) Suez Canal tanker traffic up 30% as diversion from Hormuz.
stories.consensus_narrative: The deficit is backward-looking and already priced. Brent at $85-88 reflects the reality of the Hormuz closure. The Shell CEO is stating the obvious to justify higher prices. Markets have already adjusted to the new equilibrium.
stories.contradiction: If the deficit was priced, Brent would not be sub-$90. 1.2 billion barrels is a staggering number. The entire SPR (Strategic Petroleum Reserve) of the US is ~375M barrels. The deficit is over 3x the entire US SPR. Global strategic reserves combined (~1.5B barrels) would barely cover this. If the blockade continues another month, the deficit doubles. This is not priced — it is structurally bearish for anyone short oil and structurally bullish for any oil-exposed asset. The fact that Shell's CEO — not a random analyst — is the one saying this gives it maximum credibility. He's telling the market: the supply shock is real, it's large, and it's not going away.

bet.trigger: No specific trigger needed — the number itself is the catalyst. Oil should reprice higher organically as the market digests the Shell statement. Any additional supply disruption (Trump striking Iranian power plants = production and refining capacity at risk) multiplies the impact.
bet.horizon: Next 1-2 hours for initial reprice. Full reprice over 24-48 hours. But the first 2 hours capture most of the mispricing correction.
bet.confidence: HIGH — Shell CEO is not a political source. This is the most credible quantification of the Hormuz supply shock to date.
